tldr: SpaceXAI shipped Grok 4.5 on Jul 9, its first Opus-class model since acquiring Cursor. A Jul 10 hands-on benchmark found the model cuts coding-agent cost 80% at near-frontier speed, though with a higher hallucination rate than rivals.
whats_new: One week after launch, SpaceXAI open-sourced the Rust agent harness, TUI, and tool layer behind its Grok coding CLI — the actual scaffolding behind the Jul 10 cost and hallucination numbers.
why_it_matters: The open-sourced harness lets platform engineers inspect and adopt SpaceXAI's actual tool-calling and agent-loop design directly, instead of reverse-engineering it from CLI behavior or secondhand benchmark reports.

status.detail: Launched Jul 9, independently benchmarked Jul 10, and followed by an open-sourced agent harness and tool layer on Jul 16.

beats.headline: SpaceXAI ships Grok 4.5, its first Opus-class model post Cursor acquisition
beats.summary: AINews/latent_space frames the release as SpaceXAI continuing to out-ship every other frontier lab.

beats.headline: Hands-on benchmark: 80% cheaper coding-agent runs, near-frontier speed, more hallucinations
beats.summary: Tech Times' day-two benchmark is the first independent read on Grok 4.5's coding-agent economics and reliability tradeoff.

beats.headline: SpaceXAI open-sources the Rust harness, TUI, and tool layer behind its coding CLI
beats.summary: MarkTechPost reports the actual agent scaffolding behind the CLI is now public, not just benchmarks of its output.

open_questions: Does the 80% coding-agent cost cut hold up across benchmarks beyond Tech Times' initial write-up?
How much does the higher hallucination rate cost in practice for agentic coding workflows — does it require extra verification steps that erode the price advantage?
Does SpaceXAI publish its own benchmark numbers, or does independent testing stay the only source?
What license governs the open-sourced harness, and does inspecting its tool layer explain why Grok 4.5 hallucinates more than rival coding agents?
take_for_builders: Pull the open-sourced harness and tool layer to see exactly how SpaceXAI wires tool calls and error handling in production, check its license before embedding any of it, and pair that read with your own cost/hallucination trial rather than relying on Tech Times' numbers alone.
